name: the pair is not re-anchored after the row-count stat is rebuilt
why: THE defect this spec exists for. updateH2Count() replaces .mb-row-count-stat on every filter change and re-anchors a hard-coded list of direct h2 children after the new span; anything not in that list is displaced to the front of the heading on the first keystroke. CLAUDE.md records the same trap for mb-rel-retry-*. A first-render assertion cannot see it.
grep: keeps its anchor after a filter rebuilds

name: the pair is anchored on the row-count stat, with the other h2 controls
why: The plausible alternative design: mount the pair where every other h2 control goes, right after .mb-row-count-stat. That wedges it into the middle of the artwork control run, which is drawn as ONE segmented pill selected by id prefix, so the pill splits in two. Anchoring on #mb-filter-container instead puts the pair past the end of every run. (Adding .mb-h2-table-controls to updateH2Count()'s own globalArtBtns selector does NOT reproduce this: _reanchorH2TableControls() runs later in that same function and moves it back. The guard is the anchor, not an absence from that list.)
grep: the artwork control run stays one unbroken pill

name: the two buttons are mounted loose instead of in one wrapper
why: One wrapper is what makes the re-anchor a single before() call with no DOM query, in a function that runs once per filter keystroke. Two loose children need two, and a future third control needs a third.
grep: both buttons live in one wrapper

name: the pair stays in the h1 controls bar
why: The move itself: ↔️ and 👁️ act on ONE table, so they belong beside that table's heading, where the per-sub-table pair has always been.
grep: both buttons live in one wrapper

name: updateResizeButtonState() writes the state into the glyph instead of the title
why: tests/support/browser.js's waitForRenderComplete({waitForAutoResize}) polls for a title starting with 'Restore' to know the auto-resize-on-load pass finished. Moving the wording into the button text would hang every render wait in the suite rather than failing loudly.

edits.find: resizeBtn.title = `Restore original column widths (click to toggle / ${buildShortcutHint('sa_shortcut_auto_resize', 'Ctrl+R', 'R')})`;
edits.replace:
resizeBtn.innerHTML = '↔️ Restore';
            resizeBtn.title = `Original column widths restored (click to toggle / ${buildShortcutHint('sa_shortcut_auto_resize', 'Ctrl+R', 'R')})`;

name: the rest state clears background/borderColor instead of restating them
why: uiActionBtnBaseCSS() set neither property, so '' used to fall back to the UA button default. uiHeadingGlyphBtnCSS() DOES set both, and '' removes them — leaving a transparent, borderless button where the resting grey pill should be. Purely visual, so no spec can see it; recorded here rather than left unmentioned.
